title: "Config Layers"

# Config Layers

After this page you can say which file a Git setting comes from, and set the handful of keys this book assumes.

## Three layers

| Layer | Flag | Typical file | Who |
|-------|------|--------------|-----|
| System | `--system` | `/etc/gitconfig` | every user on the machine |
| Global | `--global` | `~/.gitconfig` | you, every repo |
| Local | `--local` (default) | `.git/config` | this repo only |

Later keys **override** earlier ones. Work email in a company repo is a local `user.email`, not a second global identity you forget to switch.

```text
  wins
    ▲
    │   .git/config          local    this repo
    │   ~/.gitconfig         global   this user
    │   /etc/gitconfig       system   this machine
    │
  reads bottom → top; last value for a key wins
```

```bash
git config --list --show-origin --show-scope
git config --show-origin user.email
```

`--show-origin` prints the file that won. `--unset` removes a key at the layer you name:

```bash
git config --global --unset core.editor
```

## Set the global layer once

```bash
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global core.editor "nvim"
git config --global pull.ff only
git config --global rerere.enabled true
git config --global diff.algorithm histogram
git config --global merge.conflictstyle zdiff3
```

| Key | Why |
|-----|-----|
| `init.defaultBranch main` | `git init` creates `main`, not `master` |
| `core.editor` | `git commit` without `-m` opens this editor (`code --wait`, `vim`, `nvim`) |
| `pull.ff only` | `git pull` fast-forwards or fails; you merge or rebase on purpose |
| `rerere.enabled` | reuse recorded conflict resolutions |
| `diff.algorithm histogram` | better diffs on refactored files |
| `merge.conflictstyle zdiff3` | conflict markers include the common ancestor |

`pull.ff only` means a pull that would create a merge commit fails instead. That is safer than the old default. Chapter 11 is remotes; this setting is safe to apply now.

Leave `core.fileMode` at the default so Git records executable bits. Set it to `false` only on a filesystem that cannot store those bits.

## Repo-only overrides

```bash
cd desk-api
git config user.email "ada@work.example"
# writes .git/config
```

Inspect:

```bash
git config --local --list --show-origin
```

## `includeIf` for home vs work

```gitconfig
# ~/.gitconfig
[user]
    name = Ada Desk
    email = ada@example.com

[includeIf "gitdir:~/work/"]
    path = ~/.gitconfig-work
```

```gitconfig
# ~/.gitconfig-work
[user]
    email = ada@work.example
```

Any repo under `~/work/` picks up the work email without a per-repo command. Paths in `gitdir:` should be absolute or start with `~/`.

## See the result

```bash
git config --list --show-origin --show-scope | less
```

Identity (`user.name`, `user.email`) is the next page. Those two keys go into every commit.
